"""Our solution: Triton kernels and patches that make `soup train` lighter and faster on a T4.

The harness imports this package and calls `apply()` once, in the same process as `soup train`,
before Soup builds the model and the trainer. Every patch is class-level, looked up at call
time, and falls back to the original code outside the task's exact situation (see
`patches.py`), so Soup's regression tests pass with it applied.

Kernels of ours:
- `fused_head.py`: fused output head + cross-entropy + entropy + accuracy + per-row losses in
  vocabulary slices with an online-softmax gradient accumulator, with no [B, T, V] logits tensor
  and no full fp16 copy of the frozen output weight (about -4.4 GiB of peak memory);
- `rmsnorm.py`: fused RMSNorm forward/backward (one kernel) writing the autocast dtype, which
  removes the fp32 elementwise chain and the casts around every 4-bit projection and halves the
  stored activations downstream; the same kernel also takes the residual add that produces its
  input (`AddRMSNorm`, every residual add of the decoder; SOLUTION_DISABLE_ADDNORM=1);
- `rope.py`: fused rotary embedding of q and k, forward and backward (one kernel);
- `qgroup.py`: one NF4 dequantization launch per decoder layer and pass for its seven 4-bit
  projections (one per projection in the passes of the last layers, at the memory peak); on
  that packed buffer `fused_proj.py` runs q|k|v as one cuBLAS GEMM forward and one backward
  (SOLUTION_DISABLE_FUSED_PROJ=1; gate|up likewise, transposed, is opt-in with
  SOLUTION_FUSED_MLP=1: measured slower on the T4);
- `qlinear.py` (opt-in): the 4-bit linear layer as one dequant launch plus one cuBLAS GEMM;
- `nf4_dequant.py`: NF4 -> fp16 unpacking as a drop-in for bitsandbytes' dequant kernel, for
  projections the per-layer group does not pack (none in this task: installed only on need).
Plus `unpad.py`: padding removed inside each batch (flat forward, causal attention of all rows
in one variable-length launch of PyTorch's memory-efficient kernel per KV head, the KV heads
broadcast, not repeated, for the query heads that share them; SOLUTION_DISABLE_VARLEN=1 for one
launch per row); `lora.py`: the adapted q/v projections as one autograd node, bit-identical to
PEFT, that keeps only the layer input (dropout replayed in the backward;
SOLUTION_DISABLE_LORA=1); and `host.py`: host-side cost of the step cut with the same results
(trainer bookkeeping without module-tree walks, SOLUTION_DISABLE_BOOKKEEPING=1 switches it off;
per-step metrics fetched when they are logged instead of synced between forward and backward,
SOLUTION_DISABLE_DEFER=1).

`fp16_embed.py`: the frozen tied embedding / lm_head weight, which PEFT's
`prepare_model_for_kbit_training` upcasts from fp16 to fp32, stored back in fp16 (the same
values bit for bit; lookups still return fp32; the fused head takes its fp16 slices without a
copy): -445 MiB at the peak, SOLUTION_DISABLE_FP16_EMBED=1 switches it off.

Kept from the starter kit: `swiglu.py`, the example fused SwiGLU (does not count as ours);
`swiglu_inplace.py` is our wrapper around its kernels that writes the backward over gate/up.

Outside the training loop, `startup.py` removes work the run pays for and never uses (imports
of unused optional dependencies, a tokenizer pickled only to name a cache entry, a dtype
conversion done on the CPU, garbage-collector rescans of the import-time objects, a repeated
nvidia-smi query, a per-weight NF4 table upload, repeated chat-template renders of a row);
each patch has its own SOLUTION_DISABLE_* switch (gc.freeze: SOLUTION_DISABLE_GC_FREEZE), and
SOLUTION_DISABLE_STARTUP=1 turns them all off. (The wall-clock timeline these numbers come from
is a development tool outside the package, tools/timeline.py.)

Switches, for ablations (environment variables; with none set, the submitted solution runs). A
part that is on by default goes off with SOLUTION_DISABLE_<NAME>=1, an opt-in experiment goes on
with SOLUTION_<NAME>=1. Each is read in one place: by apply() or a helper it calls when it
removes a patch, as a constant of the module that has the code path when it picks a path
inside a patch (read when apply() imports that module); SOLUTION_VARLEN, a test knob, at each
attention call, and SOLUTION_DISABLE_SWIGLU_INPLACE also by fused_proj.py, whose opt-in MLP
node has its own copy of that backward.
- Parts: SOLUTION_DISABLE_FUSED_HEAD (the padding removal, the per-row attention and host.py go
  with it) / _UNPAD / _RMSNORM (the add + norm fusion goes with it) / _ADDNORM / _ROPE / _GROUP
  (the per-layer dequant; the LoRA node and fused_proj, which need its packed base, go with
  it) / _FUSED_PROJ / _FUSED_QKV (the q|k|v GEMM of fused_proj alone) / _LORA /
  _FP16_EMBED / _SWIGLU_INPLACE / _DEFER / _BOOKKEEPING / _DEQUANT (bitsandbytes' own kernel for
  a layer the group does not pack) = 1, and _STARTUP with every start-up patch: _GC_FREEZE and
  the rows of the `STARTUP` table below.
- Memory refinements: SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_VCHUNK (token-chunked head with a full fp16 weight
  copy) / _ROWS_ATTN (repeat_kv copies + plain SDPA per row) / _SPLIT_DEQUANT (whole-layer
  dequant also on the boundary layers) = 1.
- GPU-time refinements: SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_COMPACT (the head's gradient GEMM over all rows,
  not only the labelled ones) / _HEAD_ROWS (the head kernel's rows in element units, not
  vectorized) / _VARLEN (one attention launch per row) / _ATTN_NOCAT (per-KV-head gradient
  copies and concatenations in the attention backward) / _ROPE_TOKEN_MAJOR (RoPE gradients
  head-major, copied back by autograd) / _ROPE_ROWS (RoPE with element strides) / _LORA_CAST
  (the adapters' fp16 weights cast per projection and forward, not once per optimizer step) = 1.
- Opt-in: SOLUTION_MLP_RECOMPUTE=1 (`mlp_recompute.py`: about 1.2 GiB less peak memory for
  about +25% training-loop time; the per-layer dequant and the LoRA node go off with it);
  SOLUTION_MLP_SAVE_UP=1 (`mlp_save_up.py`: the MLP keeps up and its input and recomputes gate
  in the backward: -560 MiB of peak for +4% wall time on the T4); SOLUTION_FUSED_MLP=1
  (fused_proj.py's transposed gate|up GEMM: measured slower on the T4); SOLUTION_QLINEAR=1
  (`qlinear.py`; acts only with SOLUTION_DISABLE_GROUP=1, since the group takes every packed
  layer); SOLUTION_VARLEN=1 (the variable-length attention also on GPUs of compute capability
  8 or more, where SDPA would take flash attention: for the tests).
- Tuning: SOLUTION_HEAD_VCHUNK=N, vocabulary columns per slice of the head (default 8192).
- Start-up: SOLUTION_WARMUP_THREAD and SOLUTION_FAST_TRITON_BUILD, below.

Compilation inside the measured time: every run starts with an empty Triton cache, so each
kernel is compiled, gets a gcc-built C launcher and is loaded inside the measured wall time.
Each kernel compiles once (one specialization; RMSNorm and RoPE forward and backward are one
kernel each). The step's kernels compile in a thread of this very process, started by apply(),
while the imports run and Soup starts up and loads the model (`warmup.py`: same process, no
cache, nothing prebuilt, the compilation stays inside the measured wall time;
SOLUTION_WARMUP_THREAD=0 switches it off, `late` starts it after the imports of apply() for
comparison), and Triton's C helpers are built with gcc -O0 instead of -O3 (`triton_build.py`;
SOLUTION_FAST_TRITON_BUILD=0 switches it off).
`[solution]` lines in the training log give the wall time of the patches (a breakdown of
apply()) and of the first fused step, for the time budget outside the training loop, and one
`[solution] engaged: ...` line, after the first training step and again at exit, states for
every component whether its fast path ran in this process and how many times, and counts every
call in which an installed patch took the original code path (`engaged.py`; host counters only:
no sync, no kernel).
"""

import atexit
import os
import time

_t0 = time.perf_counter()


def _mark(label):
    # One write per line (print() writes the text and the newline separately): the warm-up
    # thread prints too, and two threads' lines must not interleave.
    print(f"[solution] {label} at {time.perf_counter() - _t0:.2f} s\n", end="", flush=True)


_lap_t = [_t0]
_exit_mark = []  # the "process exit" mark is registered (once per process)


def _in_chain(fn, marker):
    """Whether a wrapper carrying `marker` is in the patch chain of `fn`. Each of our wrappers
    keeps the function it wraps in `_original` or `_previous`, so a patch already installed
    under a later wrapper is found: apply() and each patch function install nothing twice."""
    seen = set()
    while fn is not None and id(fn) not in seen:
        seen.add(id(fn))
        if getattr(fn, marker, False):
            return True
        fn = getattr(fn, "_previous", None) or getattr(fn, "_original", None)
    return False


def _lap(label):
    """Time since the previous lap: the breakdown of apply() in the training log."""
    now = time.perf_counter()
    print(f"[solution] apply: {label} {now - _lap_t[0]:.2f} s\n", end="", flush=True)
    _lap_t[0] = now


def _warmup_mode():
    """SOLUTION_WARMUP_THREAD: "0" off, "late" started after the imports of apply(), anything
    else (the default) started at the beginning of apply()."""
    return os.environ.get("SOLUTION_WARMUP_THREAD", "1")


# Outside the training loop (startup.py): work the run pays for and never uses. One row per
# patch: the switch that turns it off, the function in startup.py, a label for the log. The
# order matters: each import here would otherwise happen inside a later one.
STARTUP = (
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_LAZY_BOTO3", "import_accelerate_without_boto3", "accelerate w/o boto3"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_LAZY_COMPILE", "import_bitsandbytes", "bnb, deferred torch.compile"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_LAZY_SKLEARN", "import_without_sklearn", "deferred scikit-learn"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_LAZY_SCIPY", "import_losses_without_scipy", "deferred SciPy (losses)"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_SHARED_MAPPING", "import_trl", "trl, shared package mapping"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_GPU_CONVERT", "patch_load_conversion", "load conversion on the GPU"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_FAST_FINGERPRINT", "patch_tokenizer_fingerprint", "tokenizer digest"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_GPU_QUERY_ONCE", "share_gpu_query", "one nvidia-smi query"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_NF4_CODE_ONCE", "share_4bit_code", "one NF4 code table"),
    ("SOLUTION_DISABLE_RENDER_ONCE", "share_chat_renders", "one render per conversation"),
)


def _startup():
    from . import startup
    from .engaged import TEXT
    from .state import installing

    applied = attempted = 0
    for switch, name, label in STARTUP:
        if os.environ.get(switch) != "1":
            attempted += 1
            with installing(f"startup.{name}"):
                result = getattr(startup, name)()
                applied += bool(result)
                _mark(f"{label}: {result}")
    TEXT["startup"] = f"{applied}/{attempted}"


def _freeze_gc(when):
    """startup.py 8: the objects alive now leave the garbage collector's scans (gc.freeze), at
    the start of apply() (the harness's imports) and at its end (apply's imports)."""
    from . import startup

    _mark(f"gc freeze ({when}): {startup.freeze_gc()} objects")


def _patch_host():
    """Host-side cost of the step (host.py): metrics fetched when they are logged instead of
    synced between forward and backward; trainer bookkeeping without module-tree walks."""
    from . import host, patches
    from .state import installing

    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_DEFER") != "1":
        with installing("defer"):
            host.defer_metrics()
            patches._host["defer"] = True
    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_BOOKKEEPING") != "1":
        with installing("bookkeeping"):
            host.trainer_bookkeeping()
            patches._host["bookkeeping"] = True


def _compiler_startup(warm, kernels):
    """Triton's start-up (every run starts with an empty Triton cache): see
    triton_build.py and warmup.py. The warm-up thread starts here, before the imports
    of apply() and startup.py, to overlap them; it compiles the kernel groups `kernels` that
    apply() is about to install."""
    from .state import installing

    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_FAST_TRITON_BUILD") != "0":
        # Triton's C launcher / cuda_utils builds at -O0 instead of -O3 (triton_build.py).
        with installing("triton_build"):
            from . import triton_build
            from .engaged import TEXT

            installed = triton_build.install()
            TEXT["build"] = triton_build.OPT_LEVEL if installed else "unavailable"
            _mark(f"Triton C helper builds at {triton_build.OPT_LEVEL}: "
                  f"{'on' if installed else 'OFF'}")
    if warm not in ("0", "late"):
        # The step's kernels compile in a thread of this process while Soup starts up and loads
        # the model (warmup.py; SOLUTION_WARMUP_THREAD=0 switches it off). Started first, so it
        # also overlaps the imports below.
        with installing("warmup"):
            from . import warmup

            warmup.start(kernels)


def apply():
    """Install everything. A later call installs what an earlier call's switches left out and
    nothing twice: the class-level patches wrap whatever method is in place, so each one is
    skipped when it is in the chain already (`_in_chain`), the warm-up thread starts once per
    process and the exit mark is registered once. Each installation step runs under
    `state.installing`: an unexpected error there leaves that component off (one
    `[solution] fallback:` line) instead of failing `soup train`; at run time every fast path
    degrades the same way (state.py)."""
    from .state import installing

    _lap_t[0] = time.perf_counter()
    startup_on = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_STARTUP") != "1"
    freeze = startup_on and os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_GC_FREEZE") != "1"
    if freeze:
        _freeze_gc("start")
    warm = _warmup_mode()
    recompute = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_MLP_RECOMPUTE") == "1"
    group = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_GROUP") != "1" and not recompute
    # Our kernel groups the training step launches, by the switches read here once: the patches
    # below install them, and the warm-up thread compiles the same ones.
    kernels = {"rmsnorm": os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_RMSNORM") != "1",
               "rope": os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_ROPE") != "1",
               "group_dequant": group,
               "fused_head": os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_FUSED_HEAD") != "1"}
    _compiler_startup(warm, kernels)
    if startup_on:
        with installing("startup"):
            _startup()
        _lap("startup.py")

    with installing("swiglu"):
        from transformers.models.qwen2 import modeling_qwen2

        from .swiglu import patch_qwen2_mlp

        if not _in_chain(modeling_qwen2.Qwen2MLP.forward, "_solution_example"):
            patch_qwen2_mlp()  # the example: works out of the box, not our own kernel
            modeling_qwen2.Qwen2MLP.forward._solution_example = True  # its wrapper, `_in_chain`
        _lap("swiglu patch (imports triton, transformers' qwen2)")

    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_SWIGLU_INPLACE") != "1":
        with installing("swiglu"):
            from .swiglu_inplace import patch_qwen2_mlp_inplace

            patch_qwen2_mlp_inplace()  # the example's kernels, its backward written over gate/up

    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_MLP_SAVE_UP") == "1":
        # Opt-in: the MLP keeps up and its input, gate is recomputed in the backward from the
        # layer's dequantized weight (one extra GEMM per layer; mlp_save_up.py).
        with installing("mlp_save_up"):
            from .mlp_save_up import patch_qwen2_mlp_save_up

            patch_qwen2_mlp_save_up()

    if recompute:
        # Opt-in: about -1.2 GiB at the peak for about +25% training-loop time (measured);
        # the scoring is a log ratio to the best team on each axis, so speed is the default.
        with installing("mlp_recompute"):
            from .mlp_recompute import patch_qwen2_mlp_recompute

            patch_qwen2_mlp_recompute()  # on top of the example: saves only the MLP input

    if kernels["rmsnorm"]:
        with installing("rmsnorm"):
            from .rmsnorm import patch_qwen2_rmsnorm

            patch_qwen2_rmsnorm()
        if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_ADDNORM") != "1":
            # every residual add inside the kernel of the norm that reads it (installed before
            # the per-layer dequant wrapper below, which wraps this layer forward)
            with installing("addnorm"):
                from .rmsnorm import patch_qwen2_add_norm

                patch_qwen2_add_norm()

    if kernels["rope"]:
        with installing("rope"):
            from .rope import patch_qwen2_rope

            patch_qwen2_rope()
    _lap("rmsnorm + rope patches")

    fused_linear = False
    if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_QLINEAR") == "1":
        # Opt-in experiment: measured neutral on the T4 (the step is not bound by bitsandbytes'
        # Python dispatch); the bit-exact dequant drop-in below is the default.
        with installing("qlinear"):
            from .qlinear import patch_bnb_linear4bit

            fused_linear = patch_bnb_linear4bit()
            _mark(f"fused 4-bit linear patch {'on' if fused_linear else 'OFF'}")

    dequant = not fused_linear and os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_DEQUANT") != "1"
    if dequant and not group:
        # bitsandbytes' own dispatch with our dequant kernel for every 4-bit projection.
        with installing("nf4_dequant"):
            from .nf4_dequant import patch_bnb_dequant

            patched = patch_bnb_dequant()
            _lap(f"nf4 dequant patch + self-check ({'on' if patched else 'OFF'})")
            _mark(f"nf4 dequant patch {'on' if patched else 'OFF'}")

    if group:
        # One dequant launch per layer and pass (7 projections at once) instead of 389 per step.
        # Our per-projection dequant (nf4_dequant.py) is installed only if a layer cannot be
        # packed (qgroup.setup_layer); in this task none is, so its kernel is never compiled.
        with installing("qgroup"):
            from . import qgroup

            qgroup.FALLBACK_DEQUANT = dequant
            qgroup.patch_group_dequant()
            _lap("group dequant patch (imports bitsandbytes)")

        if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_LORA") != "1":
            # The packed q/v projections and their adapter as one autograd node: PEFT's ops,
            # bit-identical, but only the layer input kept for the backward (the dropout is
            # replayed there); PEFT's path everywhere else.
            with installing("lora"):
                from .lora import patch_peft_lora

                patch_peft_lora()

        if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_FUSED_PROJ") != "1":
            # q|k|v and gate|up, adjacent in the packed buffer, as one GEMM each forward and
            # backward (fused_proj.py); per call, the previous path outside that situation.
            if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_FUSED_QKV") != "1":
                with installing("fused_proj"):
                    from .fused_proj import patch_qwen2_attention

                    patch_qwen2_attention()
            if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_FUSED_MLP") == "1":
                # opt-in: the transposed gate|up GEMM measured slower on the T4 (fused_proj.py)
                with installing("fused_mlp"):
                    from .fused_proj import patch_qwen2_mlp

                    patch_qwen2_mlp()

    with installing("fp16_embed"):
        from . import fp16_embed

        if fp16_embed.enabled():  # SOLUTION_DISABLE_FP16_EMBED, also read there by the warm-up
            # The frozen tied embedding / lm_head weight back in fp16 right after PEFT's fp32
            # upcast (the same values, bitwise; lookups still return fp32): -445 MiB at the peak.
            _mark("fp16 tied embedding patch "
                  f"{'on' if fp16_embed.patch_prepare_model_for_kbit_training() else 'OFF'}")

    if kernels["fused_head"]:
        # (a compute_loss patch that fails to install leaves the fused forward off too: TRL's
        # own compute_loss needs the logits)
        with installing("fused_head"):
            from .patches import patch_qwen2_causal_lm, patch_sft_compute_loss
            from .unpad import patch_sdpa_rows

            patch_sdpa_rows()
            patch_qwen2_causal_lm()
            _lap("causal LM + sdpa patches")
            try:
                patch_sft_compute_loss()
            except ImportError:  # no trl in this process (some regression tests): nothing to do
                pass
            else:
                _patch_host()
            _lap("SFTTrainer.compute_loss + host patches (imports trl)")
    if warm == "late":
        # For comparison: the same warm-up thread started after the imports above.
        with installing("warmup"):
            from . import warmup

            warmup.start(kernels)
    if freeze:
        _freeze_gc("end")
    _mark("apply done")
    if not _exit_mark:  # once per process, however often apply() runs (the tests call it a lot)
        _exit_mark.append(True)
        atexit.register(_mark, "process exit")
    from . import engaged

    # `[solution] engaged: ...`: which fast paths ran and how often (engaged.py), after the
    # first training step and at exit (registered after the mark above, so printed before it).
    engaged.install()

files.source:
"""Which fast paths of this package actually ran in this process, and how many times.

One line in the training log, printed once after the first training step (when the second step
begins, before the trainer's callbacks run, so outside the harness's timed step) and again at
exit with the totals:

    [solution] engaged: at=step1 steps=1 head=1 vchunk=1 compact=1 rows8=20 unpad=1 ... fallbacks=none

Why: every patch of this package falls back to the original code outside the task's exact
situation (that is what keeps Soup's regression tests passing), so a fallback in the measured run
would otherwise be silent. With this line the train.log of any run, the jury's hidden-rows run
included, shows that each component engaged and that no installed patch took the original path.

Cost: the counters are plain Python integers bumped on the host where each patch picks its fast
path or its fallback (a few hundred increments per step). No device sync, no extra kernel, no
tensor is read, neither when counting nor when the line is printed.

Tokens, in pipeline order: `name=count` (`off`: switched off in this process, by its SOLUTION_*
switch or because what it runs inside is off).
  at, steps       when the line is printed (step1 / exit), training steps completed
  head            training forwards through the fused output head + loss (patches.py)
  vchunk          head calls on the vocabulary-sliced path (fused_head.py; _HEAD_VCHUNK)
  compact         head calls whose hidden-gradient GEMM covered the labelled rows only
                  (_HEAD_COMPACT)
  rows8           head kernel launches with row sizes in units of 8 elements (_HEAD_ROWS)
  unpad           fused forwards with the padding removed (unpad.py; _UNPAD)
  varlen          variable-length attention launches, forward and backward, one per KV head
                  (_VARLEN); `rows_attn` (per-row attention calls) replaces nothing and is shown
                  only when varlen is off
  nocat           varlen attention backwards without per-head copies and concatenations
                  (_ATTN_NOCAT)
  lora            LoRA projection node calls (lora.py; _LORA)
  lora_cast       refreshes of the adapters' fp16 copies, about one per optimizer step
                  (_LORA_CAST)
  fused_proj      attention calls whose q|k|v ran as one GEMM node with both adapters
                  (fused_proj.py; _FUSED_PROJ / _FUSED_QKV); the last layer's split forward takes
                  the LoRA node by design, any other packed layer that does not counts as a
                  fallback (`fused_mlp`, the opt-in gate|up node, likewise)
  rmsnorm         RMSNorm kernel launches, forward and backward (rmsnorm.py; _RMSNORM)
  addnorm         residual add + RMSNorm kernel launches, forward and backward (_ADDNORM)
  rope            RoPE kernel launches, forward and backward (rope.py; _ROPE)
  group           whole-layer NF4 dequantization launches (qgroup.py; _GROUP)
  split           per-projection dequantization launches of the last layers (_SPLIT_DEQUANT)
  swiglu_inplace  MLP forwards through the in-place-backward SwiGLU wrapper (_SWIGLU_INPLACE)
  fp16_embed      tied embeddings stored in fp16 after PEFT's upcast (fp16_embed.py;
                  _FP16_EMBED)
  defer           deferred device-to-host metric fetches, one copy each (host.py; _DEFER)
  bookkeeping     trainer bookkeeping fast paths taken (host.py; _BOOKKEEPING)
  startup         start-up patches applied / attempted (startup.py; _STARTUP and the switch of
                  each patch)
  warmup          warm-up thread: ok:<kernel groups compiled>, error, running, off (warmup.py)
  build           Triton's C helper builds: -O0, unavailable, off (triton_build.py)
  fused_mlp, mlp_save_up, mlp_recompute, qlinear, nf4_dequant   opt-in / fallback paths, shown
                  only when installed (MLP forwards / 4-bit linear calls / dequant calls)
  fallbacks       `none`, or `name:count,...`: calls in which an installed patch took the
                  original code path (or, for unpad / vchunk / rows8 / fp16_embed, the
                  component's own slower path)
  disabled        only after an unexpected error: the components it turned off for the rest
                  of the process (state.DISABLED, names of state.COMPONENTS)
"""

import collections
import sys

RAN = collections.defaultdict(int)        # component -> times its fast path ran
FELL_BACK = collections.defaultdict(int)  # component -> calls that took the original path
ON = set()   # components whose patch is installed in this process (set by the patches)
TEXT = {}    # components reported as text, set by solution.apply(): startup, build
_seen = {"printed": False, "state": None, "exit_hook": False}

# The order of the line; the components that are not in ON print `off`.
ORDER = ("head", "vchunk", "compact", "rows8", "unpad", "varlen", "rows_attn", "nocat", "lora",
         "lora_cast", "fused_proj", "fused_mlp", "rmsnorm", "addnorm", "rope", "group", "split",
         "nf4_dequant", "swiglu_inplace", "mlp_save_up", "mlp_recompute", "qlinear", "fp16_embed",
         "defer", "bookkeeping")
# shown only when on
OPTIONAL = ("rows_attn", "fused_mlp", "nf4_dequant", "mlp_save_up", "mlp_recompute", "qlinear")


def _const(module, name, default=False):
    """A module constant of this package (its SOLUTION_* switch as read at import), without
    importing the module: `default` when it is not loaded."""
    loaded = sys.modules.get(f"{__package__}.{module}")
    return getattr(loaded, name, default) if loaded is not None else default


def switched_on():
    """{component: on} for this process: the installed patches, and the refinements inside them
    from their modules' switches."""
    on = {name: name in ON for name in ORDER}
    head, unpad = on["head"], on["head"] and "unpad" in ON
    on["vchunk"] = head and bool(_const("fused_head", "VOCAB_PATH"))
    on["compact"] = on["vchunk"] and bool(_const("fused_head", "COMPACT"))
    on["rows8"] = on["vchunk"] and _const("fused_head", "ROW_UNIT", 1) == 8
    on["unpad"] = unpad
    rows = unpad and bool(_const("unpad", "_ROWS_ATTENTION"))
    on["varlen"] = rows and bool(_const("unpad", "_VARLEN"))
    on["rows_attn"] = rows and not on["varlen"]  # (the per-row path is varlen's fallback)
    on["nocat"] = on["varlen"] and bool(_const("unpad", "_NOCAT"))
    on["lora_cast"] = on["lora"] and bool(_const("lora", "CAST_CACHE"))
    on["split"] = on["group"] and not _const("qgroup", "_SPLIT_OFF", True)
    return on


def _warmup():
    warmup = sys.modules.get(f"{__package__}.warmup")
    report = getattr(warmup, "_report", None) or {}
    if "error" in report:
        return "error"
    if "times" in report:
        return f"ok:{len(report['times'])}"
    if warmup is not None and getattr(warmup, "_thread", None) is not None:
        return "running"
    return "off"


def steps():
    state = _seen["state"]
    return int(getattr(state, "global_step", 0) or 0) if state is not None else 0


def _shown(name, on):
    if name == "rows_attn":  # the attention path of the flat forward when varlen is off
        return on["unpad"] and not on["varlen"]
    return name not in OPTIONAL or on[name]


def line(at):
    """The `[solution] engaged: ...` line (reads host counters only)."""
    on = switched_on()
    tokens = [f"at={at}", f"steps={steps()}"]
    for name in ORDER:
        if _shown(name, on):
            tokens.append(f"{name}={RAN[name] if on[name] else 'off'}")
    tokens += [f"startup={TEXT.get('startup', 'off')}", f"warmup={_warmup()}",
               f"build={TEXT.get('build', 'off')}"]
    names = [name for name in ORDER if FELL_BACK.get(name)]
    names += sorted(name for name in FELL_BACK if FELL_BACK[name] and name not in ORDER)
    tokens.append("fallbacks=" + (",".join(f"{name}:{FELL_BACK[name]}" for name in names)
                                  or "none"))
    # components an unexpected error turned off for the rest of the process (state.py; each also
    # printed its own `[solution] fallback:` line): shown only when there is one
    disabled = getattr(sys.modules.get(f"{__package__}.state"), "DISABLED", None)
    if disabled:
        tokens.append("disabled=" + ",".join(sorted(disabled)))
    return "[solution] engaged: " + " ".join(tokens)


def report(at, fresh_line=False):
    """`fresh_line`: start with a newline. During training the trainer's progress bar writes
    to stderr without one, and in a log of both streams the line would follow it."""
    try:
        text = line(at)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a report must never break the training run
        text = f"[solution] engaged: at={at} error={type(exc).__name__}"
    print(("\n" if fresh_line else "") + text, flush=True)


def report_at_exit():
    report("exit")


def install(register_exit=True):
    """Print the line once after the first training step (transformers' CallbackHandler, when
    the second step begins and before its callbacks run) and, with `register_exit`, at exit.
    Idempotent."""
    if register_exit and not _seen["exit_hook"]:
        import atexit

        _seen["exit_hook"] = True
        atexit.register(report_at_exit)
    try:
        from transformers.trainer_callback import CallbackHandler
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no transformers trainer here: the exit line only
        return False
    original = CallbackHandler.on_step_begin
    if getattr(original, "_solution_engaged", False):
        return True

    def on_step_begin(self, args, state, control, **kwargs):
        _seen["state"] = state
        if not _seen["printed"] and (getattr(state, "global_step", 0) or 0) >= 1:
            _seen["printed"] = True
            report("step1", fresh_line=True)
        return original(self, args, state, control, **kwargs)

    on_step_begin._solution_engaged = True
    on_step_begin._original = original
    CallbackHandler.on_step_begin = on_step_begin
    return True

"""The frozen tied embedding / output weight kept in fp16, the dtype Soup loaded it in.

On a T4 Soup loads Qwen2.5-1.5B in fp16. PEFT's `prepare_model_for_kbit_training` then upcasts
every parameter that is not 4-bit to fp32 "for stability", the tied input embedding / `lm_head`
weight [151936, 1536] included: 890 MiB, frozen, alive at the memory peak of every step (the
largest tensor of the run). An fp16 value is exact in fp32, so after that upcast an fp16 tensor
still holds the same numbers in 445 MiB. This module undoes that one upcast:

- `patch_prepare_model_for_kbit_training` wraps PEFT's function. When the model's input
  embedding was fp16 before the call and PEFT upcast it to fp32, and it is a plain, frozen
  `nn.Embedding` on CUDA whose weight IS the output head's weight (tied: one Parameter),
  `store_fp16` puts that weight back in fp16 (`param.data = fp16 copy`), after checking on the
  GPU that the copy converts back to the fp32 tensor bit for bit (otherwise nothing changes).
  The Parameter object stays the same, so `lm_head.weight is embed_tokens.weight` still holds.
- A forward hook on that embedding returns the looked-up rows as fp32: a gather from the fp16
  weight, then one exact cast (one small kernel per step), so the decoder gets the same fp32
  residual-stream input as from the fp32 weight, bit for bit.
- The output head reads fp16 values anyway. Our fused head (`fused_head.py`) cast every fp32
  vocabulary slice to fp16 before its GEMMs; from an fp16 weight it takes the slice as it is
  (the same fp16 operands without the copy, so the same logits, loss, entropy, accuracy and
  gradient, bit for bit; tested). Under autocast transformers' `lm_head` (the fallback paths)
  likewise casts the weight to fp16 first: the same values.

For the jury:
- Same values: every number of the weight is unchanged (fp16 -> fp32 is exact; checked
  bitwise on the GPU before the switch).
- Same computation, bit for bit: the embedding output is torch.equal to the fp32 lookup, the
  fused head's outputs and gradient are torch.equal with either storage, and a LoRA training
  step of a small Qwen2 through `solution.apply()` gives the same loss and LoRA gradients
  (test_fp16_embed.py, also run on the T4).
- Nothing trainable changes: the weight is frozen before and after (requires_grad False); LoRA
  weights (fp32), optimizer, adapter tensors and every file Soup writes are untouched.
- No mode is switched: Soup's config, TRL and PEFT run as before (PEFT's function itself runs
  unchanged); only this one frozen tensor is stored back in the dtype it was loaded in.
- The one observable difference: transformers' `model.dtype` (the dtype of the FIRST floating
  parameter, which is this weight) reads float16 instead of float32. Nothing in the training
  run reads it: the code of Soup's SFT trainer, TRL's SFTTrainer, transformers' Trainer and
  Qwen2 model, PEFT's LoRA set-up and saving, and accelerate was checked; the attention mask and
  rotary dtypes come from the embedding output, which stays fp32; the trainer's FLOP count and
  PEFT's parameter counts read numbers of elements, not dtypes.
- Memory at load: the fp16 copy exists next to the fp32 weight for a moment, the same transient
  as PEFT's own upcast a moment earlier (peak allocated during `prepare` 1,981 -> 2,005 MiB on
  the real model), far below the training peak; afterwards 1,536 -> 1,091 MiB are allocated.
- Measured on the real Qwen2.5-1.5B (4-bit, fp16, RTX 4080 with deterministic algorithms, so
  that two runs of the same code agree): three AdamW steps through `solution.apply()` give the
  same losses, LoRA gradients and LoRA weights bit for bit with either storage.
The frozen RMSNorm weights and q/k/v biases (also upcast, 0.6 MiB together) stay fp32: nothing
to gain there.

SOLUTION_DISABLE_FP16_EMBED=1 switches it off (the weight stays fp32, as PEFT leaves it).
"""

import functools
import os
import weakref

import torch

from .engaged import FELL_BACK, ON, RAN
from .state import DISABLED, fallback

# (weak reference to the embedding module, hook handle, MiB saved) for every embedding this module
# stored in fp16. Weak: a strong reference would keep the module and its fp16 weight (445 MiB
# here) alive after the model is gone (the handle itself holds only weak references).
_applied = []


def enabled():
    return os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_FP16_EMBED") != "1"


def head_weight_dtype(half):
    """The dtype of the output weight the fused head gets in training, for the warm-up's
    compile: fp16 when this module stores it (the fp16 path of a T4, where Soup loads the model
    in fp16 and trains under fp16 autocast, with the switch on), fp32 (PEFT's upcast) otherwise."""
    return torch.float16 if half == torch.float16 and enabled() else torch.float32


def tied_embedding(model):
    """(embedding module, weight) when `model`'s input embedding is a plain `nn.Embedding` on
    CUDA, without max_norm (which would write the weight), whose weight is the same Parameter as
    the output head's weight; None for anything else."""
    try:
        emb = model.get_input_embeddings()
        head = model.get_output_embeddings()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - not a transformers model, or no embeddings: not ours
        return None
    if type(emb) is not torch.nn.Embedding or head is None:
        return None
    weight = emb.weight
    if (not isinstance(weight, torch.nn.Parameter) or getattr(head, "weight", None) is not weight
            or weight.dim() != 2 or not weight.is_cuda or emb.max_norm is not None):
        return None
    return emb, weight


def bitwise_equal(w16, w32, rows=2048):
    """Whether the fp16 tensor converts back to the fp32 one bit for bit (fp32 bit patterns
    compared, so even the sign of a zero counts), in blocks of rows (temporaries of 12 MiB at
    this task's width)."""
    differs = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.bool, device=w32.device)
    for start in range(0, w32.shape[0], rows):
        back = w16[start:start + rows].float().view(torch.int32)
        differs |= (back != w32[start:start + rows].view(torch.int32)).any()
    return not bool(differs)


def _fp32_output(module, args, output):
    """Forward hook of an embedding stored in fp16: the looked-up rows as fp32, exactly the
    values the fp32 weight gives (fp16 -> fp32 is exact)."""
    if isinstance(output, torch.Tensor) and output.dtype == torch.float16:
        return output.float()
    return output


def store_fp16(model, expected=None, clear_cache=True):
    """Store `model`'s tied, frozen fp32 embedding / output weight in fp16 when that loses
    nothing (bitwise check); its lookups then return fp32 as before. `expected`: the weight must
    be this Parameter. Returns the MiB saved (0: nothing changed)."""
    found = tied_embedding(model)
    if found is None:
        return 0
    emb, weight = found
    if (expected is not None and weight is not expected) or weight.dtype != torch.float32 \
            or weight.requires_grad or not weight.is_contiguous():
        return 0
    w16 = weight.data.to(torch.float16)
    if not bitwise_equal(w16, weight.data):
        return 0
    saved = weight.numel() * 2 / 2**20
    # the hook first (a no-op while the weight is fp32): an error between the two steps cannot
    # leave an fp16 weight whose lookups return fp16
    handle = emb.register_forward_hook(_fp32_output)
    weight.data = w16  # the same Parameter object: still tied to the output head
    _applied.append((weakref.ref(emb), handle, saved))
    if clear_cache:
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()  # the freed fp32 weight, as PEFT does after its own casts
    return saved


def patch_prepare_model_for_kbit_training():
    """Wrap PEFT's `prepare_model_for_kbit_training` (in each PEFT namespace that exports it):
    after it ran, the tied embedding it upcast from fp16 goes back to fp16 (`store_fp16`)."""
    try:
        import peft
        import peft.utils as peft_utils
        from peft.utils import other
    except ImportError:
        return False
    original = getattr(other, "prepare_model_for_kbit_training", None)
    if original is None:
        return False
    if getattr(original, "_solution_fp16_embed", False):
        return True

    @functools.wraps(original)
    def prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model, *args, **kwargs):
        # (graceful degradation, state.py: an unexpected error in our steps before and after
        # PEFT's own function leaves the weight as PEFT leaves it; PEFT's call is not ours)
        loaded = None
        try:
            found = tied_embedding(model)
            loaded = found[1] if found is not None and found[1].dtype == torch.float16 else None
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
            if not fallback("fp16_embed", exc):
                raise
        result = original(model, *args, **kwargs)
        saved = 0
        if loaded is not None and "fp16_embed" not in DISABLED:
            # PEFT's upcast of a weight loaded in fp16: back to fp16
            try:
                clear = kwargs.get("auto_clear_cache", args[2] if len(args) > 2 else True)
                saved = store_fp16(result, expected=loaded, clear_cache=bool(clear))
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("fp16_embed", exc):
                    raise
            from . import _mark

            _mark("tied embedding/lm_head kept in fp16 after PEFT's upcast: "
                  + (f"-{saved:.0f} MiB" if saved else "not applicable"))
        if saved:  # engaged.py's counters (not stored: no fp16 tied weight, or not exact)
            RAN["fp16_embed"] += 1
        else:
            FELL_BACK["fp16_embed"] += 1
        return result

    prepare_model_for_kbit_training._solution_fp16_embed = True
    prepare_model_for_kbit_training._original = original
    for namespace in (peft, peft_utils, other):
        if getattr(namespace, "prepare_model_for_kbit_training", None) is original:
            namespace.prepare_model_for_kbit_training = prepare_model_for_kbit_training
    ON.add("fp16_embed")
    return True

"""Fused output head + causal-LM loss without a [B, T, V] logits tensor.

The base run materializes fp16 logits [4, 512, 151936], upcasts them to fp32 for the loss and
keeps three fp32 copies of that shape alive through backward (about 4 GiB on this task). Here
the head never holds more than one slice of the logits: one Triton kernel per row computes
everything that is read from the logits (log-sum-exp, cross-entropy of the target, Shannon
entropy, argmax) and overwrites the slice in place with softmax weights, and cuBLAS turns those
into the gradient of the hidden states. Only the [N, H] fp16 hidden gradient survives the
forward; no graph over the logits exists.

Default path (`FusedHeadLossVocab`): the head walks the VOCABULARY in slices of VOCAB_CHUNK
columns, all tokens at once, so it never needs an fp16 copy of the whole frozen fp32 weight
(445 MiB, alive on top of every saved activation at the peak of the step): only one 24 MiB
slice of it (VOCAB_CHUNK = 8192 columns) is cast at a time. With the weight stored in fp16
(`fp16_embed.py`, the default on the T4) the slices are views of it: no cast and no buffer, the
same fp16 GEMM operands. Per slice: cuBLAS writes the logits [N, VOCAB_CHUNK]; the kernel
continues each row's online log-sum-exp / entropy / argmax from the previous slices, rescales the
row's fp32 gradient accumulator when its running max moved, and rewrites the row in place as
exp(z - running max); cuBLAS adds that times the weight slice to the accumulator (fp32 output),
as in the online-softmax accumulation of FlashAttention. A last launch turns the accumulator into
dH = acc / sum - W16[target] (0 on unlabelled rows). With VOCAB_CHUNK a multiple of BLOCK_V the
row statistics (and so loss, entropy, argmax) are computed in exactly the same order as by the
token-chunked kernel below.

The accumulator covers the labelled rows only (SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_COMPACT=1: all rows, as
before). The hidden gradient of an unlabelled (prompt) row is 0, and 40-55% of the rows of this
task are prompt. With the gradient on, the rows are put labelled-first (`labelled_first`: the
order from a cumsum on the GPU, the number of labelled rows from the host sync the padding
removal makes anyway, `patches.py`; one gather of the fp16 hidden states and the targets), and
each slice's accumulator GEMM takes only the n_labelled leading rows of the logits slice. Every
slice's logits GEMM and kernel still run over all rows: loss, the entropy of every position and
the accuracy are bit-identical (the same rows through the same GEMM, in another order; tested),
and the per-row outputs and the gradient are put back in the input order at the end. The
accumulator GEMM has fewer rows, which cuBLAS may tile differently: the gradient is NOT bit for
bit the all-rows one; the test bounds it by one fp16 ulp of the largest element (atol =
max|dH| * 2^-10, rtol 1e-3), and measured on task shapes at most 0.2% of the elements differ,
by 1-3 ulp each (checks 5-7 compare at 3% / 0.5%). Measured on the Kaggle T4 (per-kernel profiles of
adjacent runs, two sessions): accumulator GEMM 21.1 -> 14.8 and 18.8 -> 13.6 ms per step (it
does not halve: fewer rows tile less evenly over the 40 SMs), peak memory and eval loss
unchanged.

Token-chunked path (`FusedHeadLoss`, SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_VCHUNK=1): `chunk` tokens at a time
against the full fp16 weight; the row kernel writes `p - onehot(target)` in place.

Ideas: chunked head + loss as in Soup's own `stream_loss_chunk`, the fused linear-cross-entropy of
Liger-Kernel (Hsu et al., 2024), Cut Cross-Entropy (Wijmans et al., 2024), online softmax
(Milakov & Gimelshein, 2018) and FlashAttention's rescaled accumulator (Dao et al., 2022). The
code is ours.

Formulas match the base exactly in semantics:
- loss  = sum_{t: y_t != -100} (lse_t - z_{t, y_t}) / num_items_in_batch   (transformers
  `ForCausalLMLoss`; `/ #labelled` when num_items_in_batch is None);
- entropy_t = lse_t - sum_v p_v z_v for EVERY position (TRL averages it with attention_mask);
- correct_t = [argmax_v z_{t,v} == y_t] for labelled positions (TRL's mean_token_accuracy);
- per-token loss for Soup's rewind log, 0 where y_t == -100.
"""

import os

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from .engaged import FELL_BACK, RAN

BLOCK_V = 4096      # vocabulary slice per loop iteration
NUM_WARPS = 8
DEFAULT_CHUNK = 256  # tokens per logits chunk (token-chunked path): 256 x 151936 x 2 B = 74 MiB
# Columns per vocabulary slice: 8192 x 1536 fp16 = 24 MiB of weight + [N, 8192] fp16 logits,
# 19 slices for Qwen2.5's 151936 tokens.
VOCAB_CHUNK = int(os.environ.get("SOLUTION_HEAD_VCHUNK", "8192"))
BLOCK_H = 512       # hidden-size slice of the accumulator rows
VOCAB_PATH = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_VCHUNK") != "1"
# The hidden-gradient GEMM over the labelled rows only (see `labelled_first`).
COMPACT = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_COMPACT") != "1"
# Row sizes/strides passed to the vocabulary kernel in units of 8 elements, so its row loads and
# stores vectorize (as RoPE's did: 3.75 -> 1.65 ms per step there); SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_ROWS=1
# passes element units as before. Not bit-identical: the vectorized layout changes the order of
# the in-row fp32 reductions (last-bit differences, within the tests' tolerances). Measured on
# the T4 (session t3a, per-kernel profiles of adjacent runs): this kernel 3.50 -> 2.35 and
# 3.26 -> 2.37 ms per step; eval loss 2.0498 either way, peak memory unchanged.
ROW_UNIT = 1 if os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_ROWS") == "1" else 8


@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n_cols", "col0", "stride_row", "n_hidden", "stride_acc",
                               "stride_w", "write_grad", "first", "last", "finalize"])
def fused_head_vocab_kernel(logits_ptr, targets_ptr, stats_ptr, best_idx_ptr, acc_ptr, w_ptr,
                            grad_ptr, loss_ptr, entropy_ptr, correct_ptr, n_cols, col0,
                            stride_row, n_hidden, stride_acc, stride_w, write_grad, first, last,
                            finalize, BLOCK: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
                            UNIT: tl.constexpr):
    """One program per token row. finalize == 0: one vocabulary slice [col0, col0 + n_cols) of
    the row (statistics, then, for labelled rows when write_grad != 0, the accumulator rescale
    and exp(z - m) in place). finalize != 0: dH = acc / s - W16[target] (0 when unlabelled).
    n_cols, stride_row, n_hidden, stride_acc and stride_w come in units of UNIT elements: with
    UNIT = 8 every row and every bound is provably a multiple of 8, so the row loads and stores
    vectorize (16 bytes of fp16 per access instead of 2)."""
    n_cols = n_cols * UNIT
    stride_row = stride_row * UNIT
    n_hidden = n_hidden * UNIT
    stride_acc = stride_acc * UNIT
    stride_w = stride_w * UNIT
    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
    target = tl.load(targets_ptr + row)
    labelled = target >= 0
    sp = stats_ptr + row * 5  # running max m, sum s, entropy numerator t, best logit, z_target
    acc_row = acc_ptr + row * stride_acc
    if finalize != 0:
        s = tl.load(sp + 1)
        w_row = w_ptr + tl.maximum(target, 0) * stride_w
        g_row = grad_ptr + row * n_hidden
        for h in range(0, n_hidden, BLOCK_H):
            offs = h + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
            hmask = offs < n_hidden
            # unlabelled rows read nothing: with the labelled rows compacted (FusedHeadLossVocab)
            # the accumulator has no row for them
            lmask = hmask & labelled
            a = tl.load(acc_row + offs, mask=lmask, other=0.0)
            # the fp16 value of W[target] the GEMMs used: its rounding cancels exactly
            w16 = tl.load(w_row + offs, mask=lmask, other=0.0).to(tl.float16).to(tl.float32)
            g = tl.where(labelled, a / s - w16, 0.0)
            tl.store(g_row + offs, g.to(grad_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=hmask)
    else:
        base = logits_ptr + row * stride_row
        not_first = first == 0
        m = tl.load(sp + 0, mask=not_first, other=-float("inf"))
        s = tl.load(sp + 1, mask=not_first, other=0.0)
        t = tl.load(sp + 2, mask=not_first, other=0.0)
        best = tl.load(sp + 3, mask=not_first, other=-float("inf"))
        zt = tl.load(sp + 4, mask=not_first, other=0.0)
        best_idx = tl.load(best_idx_ptr + row, mask=not_first, other=0)
        m_old = m
        for start in range(0, n_cols, BLOCK):
            offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
            mask = offs < n_cols
            z = tl.load(base + offs, mask=mask, other=-float("inf")).to(tl.float32)
            block_max = tl.max(z, axis=0)
            m_new = tl.maximum(m, block_max)
            alpha = tl.exp(m - m_new)
            e = tl.exp(z - m_new)
            s = s * alpha + tl.sum(e, axis=0)
            t = t * alpha + tl.sum(e * tl.where(mask, z, 0.0), axis=0)
            m = m_new
            block_idx = tl.argmax(z, axis=0, tie_break_left=True)
            better = block_max > best
            best_idx = tl.where(better, col0 + start + block_idx, best_idx)
            best = tl.maximum(best, block_max)
        rel = target - col0
        here = labelled & (rel >= 0) & (rel < n_cols)
        zt = tl.where(here, tl.load(base + rel, mask=here, other=0.0).to(tl.float32), zt)
        tl.store(sp + 0, m)
        tl.store(sp + 1, s)
        tl.store(sp + 2, t)
        tl.store(sp + 3, best)
        tl.store(sp + 4, zt)
        tl.store(best_idx_ptr + row, best_idx)
        if last != 0:
            ls = tl.log(s)
            lse = m + ls
            tl.store(entropy_ptr + row, lse - t / s)
            # ls + (m - zt), not lse - zt: m and zt are fp16 logit values, so m - zt is exact in
            # fp32 and a confident token keeps the low bits of log(s), as PyTorch's
            # (z - max) - log(sum) does (lse - zt would round log(s) away against m ~ 25).
            tl.store(loss_ptr + row, tl.where(labelled, ls + (m - zt), 0.0))
            hit = best_idx.to(tl.int64) == target
            tl.store(correct_ptr + row, (labelled & hit).to(tl.int32))
        if labelled & (write_grad != 0):
            if not_first & (m > m_old):  # earlier slices were weighted by exp(z - m_old)
                scale = tl.exp(m_old - m)
                for h in range(0, n_hidden, BLOCK_H):
                    offs = h + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
                    hmask = offs < n_hidden
                    a = tl.load(acc_row + offs, mask=hmask, other=0.0)
                    tl.store(acc_row + offs, a * scale, mask=hmask)
            for start in range(0, n_cols, BLOCK):
                offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
                mask = offs < n_cols
                z = tl.load(base + offs, mask=mask, other=-float("inf")).to(tl.float32)
                tl.store(base + offs, tl.exp(z - m).to(logits_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)


@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n_rows", "n_cols", "stride_row", "write_grad"])
def fused_head_rows_kernel(logits_ptr, targets_ptr, loss_ptr, entropy_ptr, correct_ptr,
                           n_rows, n_cols, stride_row, write_grad, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    """Token-chunked path. One program per row of the logits chunk. Pass 1 streams the row once
    for the online log-sum-exp, the entropy numerator and the first argmax; pass 2 (labelled
    rows only, when write_grad != 0) rewrites the row in place as softmax(z) - onehot(target)."""
    row = tl.program_id(0)
    base = logits_ptr + row.to(tl.int64) * stride_row
    target = tl.load(targets_ptr + row)
    labelled = target >= 0

    m = -float("inf")
    s = 0.0
    t = 0.0
    best = -float("inf")
    best_idx = 0
    for start in range(0, n_cols, BLOCK):
        offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
        mask = offs < n_cols
        z = tl.load(base + offs, mask=mask, other=-float("inf")).to(tl.float32)
        block_max = tl.max(z, axis=0)
        m_new = tl.maximum(m, block_max)
        alpha = tl.exp(m - m_new)
        e = tl.exp(z - m_new)
        s = s * alpha + tl.sum(e, axis=0)
        t = t * alpha + tl.sum(e * tl.where(mask, z, 0.0), axis=0)
        m = m_new
        block_idx = tl.argmax(z, axis=0, tie_break_left=True)
        better = block_max > best
        best_idx = tl.where(better, start + block_idx, best_idx)
        best = tl.maximum(best, block_max)

    ls = tl.log(s)
    lse = m + ls
    tl.store(entropy_ptr + row, lse - t / s)
    z_target = tl.load(base + target, mask=labelled, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
    # ls + (m - z_target): exact difference of two fp16 logit values, so a confident token keeps
    # the low bits of log(s) as PyTorch's (z - max) - log(sum) does.
    tl.store(loss_ptr + row, tl.where(labelled, ls + (m - z_target), 0.0))
    hit = best_idx.to(tl.int64) == target
    tl.store(correct_ptr + row, (labelled & hit).to(tl.int32))

    if labelled & (write_grad != 0):
        for start in range(0, n_cols, BLOCK):
            offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
            mask = offs < n_cols
            z = tl.load(base + offs, mask=mask, other=-float("inf")).to(tl.float32)
            grad = tl.exp(z - lse) - (offs == target).to(tl.float32)
            tl.store(base + offs, grad.to(logits_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)


def launch_vocab(n_rows, logits, targets, stats, best_idx, acc, weight, grad, token_loss,
                 token_entropy, correct, n_cols, col0, stride_row, n_hidden, write_grad, first,
                 last, finalize):
    """The one launch site of the vocabulary-sliced kernel (training and the warm-up thread).
    Sizes and strides go in units of ROW_UNIT elements when they all are multiples of it (every
    launch of this task: slices of 8192 and 4480 columns, hidden size 1536, so still one
    specialization), else of 1. Returns the unit."""
    sizes = (n_cols, stride_row, n_hidden, acc.stride(0), weight.stride(0))
    unit = ROW_UNIT if all(size % ROW_UNIT == 0 for size in sizes) else 1
    n_cols, stride_row, n_hidden, stride_acc, stride_w = (size // unit for size in sizes)
    fused_head_vocab_kernel[(n_rows,)](
        logits, targets, stats, best_idx, acc, weight, grad, token_loss, token_entropy, correct,
        n_cols, col0, stride_row, n_hidden, stride_acc, stride_w, int(write_grad), int(first),
        int(last), int(finalize), BLOCK=BLOCK_V, BLOCK_H=BLOCK_H, UNIT=unit,
        num_warps=NUM_WARPS)
    return unit


def _count_rows8(unit):
    """engaged.py's `rows8` counter: a training launch of the vocabulary kernel in units of 8,
    or with element units although they are on (a size that is not a multiple of 8)."""
    if unit == 8:
        RAN["rows8"] += 1
    elif ROW_UNIT == 8:
        FELL_BACK["rows8"] += 1


def launch_rows(logits, targets, token_loss, token_entropy, correct, write_grad):
    """The one launch site of the kernel (training and the warm-up thread): logits [rows, V]
    with contiguous rows; the four per-row tensors are [rows] slices."""
    rows, vocab = logits.shape
    fused_head_rows_kernel[(rows,)](
        logits, targets, token_loss, token_entropy, correct, rows, vocab, logits.stride(0),
        int(write_grad), BLOCK=BLOCK_V, num_warps=NUM_WARPS)


def _denominator(num_items, labelled_count):
    if num_items is None:
        return labelled_count.clamp(min=1).to(torch.float32)
    if torch.is_tensor(num_items):
        return num_items.to(torch.float32)
    return torch.tensor(float(num_items), device=labelled_count.device)


def _head_backward(ctx, grad_loss):
    (grad_hidden,) = ctx.saved_tensors
    scale = grad_loss.to(torch.float32) / ctx.denom
    # num_items_in_batch = 0 (no labelled target in the batch): the base's loss is 0 / 0 = NaN
    # but its gradient is exactly 0 (cross-entropy writes none on ignored rows), and here
    # grad_hidden is all zeros; 0 * inf would be NaN. Same value whenever denom != 0, no sync.
    scale = torch.where(ctx.denom != 0, scale, 0.0)
    return (grad_hidden.to(torch.float32) * scale).to(ctx.out_dtype)


def labelled_first(labelled, n_labelled):
    """The order that puts the labelled rows first (each group in its original order), without
    a host sync: (dest, src) with row r of the input at position dest[r] of the reordered rows
    and src the inverse (reordered row i is input row src[i])."""
    n = labelled.shape[0]
    pos = torch.arange(n, device=labelled.device)
    seen = torch.cumsum(labelled, 0)  # labelled rows up to and including r (int64)
    dest = torch.where(labelled, seen - 1, pos - seen + n_labelled)
    src = torch.empty_like(dest).index_copy_(0, dest, pos)
    return dest, src


class FusedHeadLossVocab(torch.autograd.Function):
    """loss, per-token loss, per-token entropy, per-token correctness from hidden states and the
    (frozen) output weight, walking the vocabulary in slices. Saves only the fp16 hidden
    gradient; holds one fp16 weight slice and one [N, vocab_chunk] logits slice at a time.

    The hidden gradient of an unlabelled row is 0: with `n_labelled` (the number of rows with
    target >= 0, a host int; counted here with one host sync when it is not given) the rows are
    reordered labelled-first (`labelled_first`), every slice's logits GEMM and kernel still run
    over all rows (the statistics of every row, unchanged), but the accumulator GEMM and the
    accumulator itself cover only the n_labelled leading rows. The per-row outputs and the
    gradient are put back in the input order at the end (SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_COMPACT=1: the
    accumulator over all rows, as before)."""

    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, hidden, weight, targets, num_items, vocab_chunk, need_grad, n_labelled):
        n_tokens, hidden_size = hidden.shape
        vocab = weight.shape[0]
        device = hidden.device
        h16 = hidden.detach().to(torch.float16).contiguous()
        weight = weight.detach()
        targets = targets.contiguous()
        vchunk = max(1, min(int(vocab_chunk), vocab))
        labelled = targets >= 0

        # rows of the accumulator: all of them, or only the labelled ones put first
        n_grad, dest, rows_targets = n_tokens, None, targets
        if need_grad and COMPACT and n_tokens > 0:
            if n_labelled is None:
                n_labelled = int(labelled.sum())
            n_grad = int(n_labelled)
            if 0 < n_grad < n_tokens:
                dest, src = labelled_first(labelled, n_grad)
                h16 = h16.index_select(0, src)
                rows_targets = targets.index_select(0, src)
                RAN["compact"] += 1

        token_loss = torch.empty(n_tokens, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        token_entropy = torch.empty_like(token_loss)
        correct = torch.empty(n_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        stats = torch.empty(n_tokens, 5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        best_idx = torch.empty(n_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        grad_hidden = torch.empty_like(h16) if need_grad else None
        # (unused without labelled rows: one row, for the launch's row stride only)
        acc = torch.empty(n_grad if need_grad and n_grad > 0 else 1, hidden_size,
                          dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        grad_arg = grad_hidden if need_grad else h16
        if n_tokens > 0:
            logits_buf = torch.empty(n_tokens * vchunk, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)
            # An fp16 weight (the tied embedding as fp16_embed.py stores it): each slice of
            # rows is a contiguous [cols, H] fp16 matrix already, the GEMM operand as it is.
            # Otherwise (fp32): each slice cast into one reused fp16 buffer, the same values.
            sliced = weight.dtype == torch.float16 and weight.is_contiguous()
            w16_buf = None if sliced else torch.empty(vchunk * hidden_size, dtype=torch.float16,
                                                      device=device)
            for start in range(0, vocab, vchunk):
                cols = min(vchunk, vocab - start)
                if sliced:
                    w16 = weight[start:start + cols]
                else:
                    w16 = w16_buf[:cols * hidden_size].view(cols, hidden_size)
                    w16.copy_(weight[start:start + cols])
                logits = logits_buf[:n_tokens * cols].view(n_tokens, cols)
                torch.mm(h16, w16.t(), out=logits)
                _count_rows8(launch_vocab(
                    n_tokens, logits, rows_targets, stats, best_idx, acc, weight, grad_arg,
                    token_loss, token_entropy, correct, cols, start, logits.stride(0),
                    hidden_size, need_grad, start == 0, start + cols >= vocab, False))
                if need_grad and n_grad > 0:
                    torch.addmm(acc, logits[:n_grad], w16, beta=0 if start == 0 else 1,
                                out_dtype=torch.float32, out=acc)
            del logits_buf, w16_buf, logits, w16
            if need_grad:
                _count_rows8(launch_vocab(
                    n_tokens, h16, rows_targets, stats, best_idx, acc, weight, grad_hidden,
                    token_loss, token_entropy, correct, 0, 0, 0, hidden_size, True, False, False,
                    True))
        del acc, stats, best_idx, h16
        if dest is not None:  # back to the input order
            token_loss = token_loss.index_select(0, dest)
            token_entropy = token_entropy.index_select(0, dest)
            correct = correct.index_select(0, dest)
            grad_hidden = grad_hidden.index_select(0, dest)

        denom = _denominator(num_items, labelled.sum())
        loss = token_loss.sum() / denom
        correct = correct.to(torch.bool)
        ctx.denom = denom
        ctx.out_dtype = hidden.dtype
        if need_grad:
            ctx.save_for_backward(grad_hidden)
        ctx.mark_non_differentiable(token_loss, token_entropy, correct)
        return loss, token_loss, token_entropy, correct

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_loss, _grad_token_loss, _grad_entropy, _grad_correct):
        return _head_backward(ctx, grad_loss), None, None, None, None, None, None


class FusedHeadLoss(torch.autograd.Function):
    """Token-chunked path: the same outputs from `chunk` tokens at a time against a full fp16
    copy of the weight (no copy when the weight is stored in fp16)."""

    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, hidden, weight, targets, num_items, chunk, need_grad):
        n_tokens, hidden_size = hidden.shape
        vocab = weight.shape[0]
        h16 = hidden.detach().to(torch.float16).contiguous()
        w16 = weight.detach().to(torch.float16)  # the weight itself when it is stored in fp16
        targets = targets.contiguous()

        token_loss = torch.empty(n_tokens, dtype=torch.float32, device=hidden.device)
        token_entropy = torch.empty_like(token_loss)
        correct = torch.empty(n_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device=hidden.device)
        grad_hidden = torch.empty_like(h16) if need_grad else None
        buf = torch.empty(min(chunk, n_tokens), vocab, dtype=torch.float16, device=hidden.device)
        labelled = targets >= 0

        for start in range(0, n_tokens, chunk):
            end = min(start + chunk, n_tokens)
            rows = end - start
            logits = buf[:rows]
            torch.mm(h16[start:end], w16.t(), out=logits)
            launch_rows(logits, targets[start:end], token_loss[start:end],
                        token_entropy[start:end], correct[start:end], need_grad)
            if need_grad:
                torch.mm(logits, w16, out=grad_hidden[start:end])
                # Unlabelled rows still hold logits, not gradients, and their product with W
                # may even overflow fp16: replace those rows (not multiply) with 0.
                grad_hidden[start:end].masked_fill_(~labelled[start:end, None], 0)

        denom = _denominator(num_items, labelled.sum())
        loss = token_loss.sum() / denom
        correct = correct.to(torch.bool)
        ctx.denom = denom
        ctx.out_dtype = hidden.dtype
        if need_grad:
            ctx.save_for_backward(grad_hidden)
        ctx.mark_non_differentiable(token_loss, token_entropy, correct)
        return loss, token_loss, token_entropy, correct

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_loss, _grad_token_loss, _grad_entropy, _grad_correct):
        return _head_backward(ctx, grad_loss), None, None, None, None, None


def fused_head_loss(hidden, weight, targets, num_items=None, vocab_chunk=None, *,
                    token_chunk=None, n_labelled=None):
    """hidden [N, H] (fp16/fp32, may require grad), weight [V, H] frozen, targets [N] int64
    already shifted (-100 = ignore). Returns (loss, token_loss[N], token_entropy[N], correct[N]).
    Vocabulary-sliced by default; `token_chunk=` (or SOLUTION_DISABLE_HEAD_VCHUNK=1) selects the
    token-chunked path. `n_labelled`: the host count of targets >= 0, when the caller has it
    (saves the vocabulary-sliced path a host sync); it must be exact."""
    need_grad = torch.is_grad_enabled() and hidden.requires_grad
    if token_chunk is None and VOCAB_PATH and weight.dim() == 2 and weight.stride(1) == 1:
        RAN["vchunk"] += 1
        return FusedHeadLossVocab.apply(hidden, weight, targets, num_items,
                                        vocab_chunk or VOCAB_CHUNK, need_grad, n_labelled)
    if VOCAB_PATH:
        FELL_BACK["vchunk"] += 1  # the token-chunked head although the vocabulary path is on
    return FusedHeadLoss.apply(hidden, weight, targets, num_items, token_chunk or DEFAULT_CHUNK,
                               need_grad)
